subject: Inference SLOs & deployment plan — LumenLogic discovery follow-up
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@lumenlogic.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Inference SLOs & deployment plan — LumenLogic discovery follow-up

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the time today. Short recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Top pain points you shared:
- User-facing completions need consistent 95th %-tile latency <= 120ms for short prompts (~32 tokens).
- Spiky burst traffic from search/autocomplete (peaks to ~2.5k rps for ~3-5m windows).
- Cost sensitivity for steady-state traffic; willing to trade small latency increases for 30-40% cost reduction.
- Regulatory requirement: data residency in us-east for PII-sensitive endpoints.

Agreed goals:
- Proof-of-concept (3-week) to validate 95th%-tile latency at target throughput and quantify unit cost.
- Provide a recommended topology for production (Dedicated GPU pool + cross-region failover).
- Deliver observability dashboard and a small eval suite (prompt set + perf tests).

Technical notes / what we need from you:
1) Typical request shape (avg/95th token length) and percent of calls that are short completions vs long.
2) 14-day peak/typical RPS numbers and any upcoming events that could spike traffic.
3) Any internal infra constraints (VPC peering, egress rules) for Private deployment.

Attachments: I’m attaching the load curve template we discussed and an initial sketch of the MVP topology (lumenlogic-load-curve.csv, mvp-topology-sketch.png).

Proposed next steps (we can adjust after you confirm numbers):
- You: share the token-length distribution and last 14 days RPS export (by EOD Wed).
- Us: produce a short POC plan (test harness, target models, latency targets) by Thu.
- Schedule: POC kickoff the week of Jun 26 (three weeks).

If that aligns I’ll loop in Solutions (Mina) to validate the topology and Ops (Marissa) for the observability runbook.

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

From: Daniel Park <daniel@lumenlogic.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@lumenlogic.com
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference SLOs & deployment plan — LumenLogic discovery follow-up

Karthik — this is great, thanks for pulling together. Quick confirmations and the data you asked for: 

- Token distribution (short vs long): ~72% short (<40 tokens), 20% medium (40-256 tokens), 8% long (>256).
- Typical steady-state: 450 rps. Peak (recent marketing push): sustained ~2.3k rps for ~6 minutes, occasional 4k rps spikes for <1 minute.
- Average prompt size for short completions: 18 tokens; avg response ~28 tokens.
- We can share a CSV of the last 14 days (attached).

Notes: we need the POC to run in us-east only (for data residency). We can provide a read-only monitoring token and a Datadog endpoint for the POC.

Confirming POC kickoff week of Jun 26 works for us. Can you confirm what model variants you intend to test versus cost-estimate ranges?

Thanks — Daniel

Attachments: lumenlogic-load-curve.csv

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 08:25:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: LumenLogic POC topology suggestions

Internal notes — summary from Daniel's numbers and suggested approach for the POC: 

Numbers to plan for:
- Steady 450 rps, 95th%-tile short-latency target <= 120ms (32-token context).
- Planning headroom to 3k sustained and ability to absorb 4k 1-minute spikes.

POC topology (recommended):
1) Dedicated pool in us-east (2 x 8xH100 equiv. split across 2 instances for redundancy)
   - Continuous batching with 50-75ms batch window for cost-efficiency.
   - KV prefix cache enabled for short completions — expect ~18-25% cost savings and latency improvement for repeated prompts.
2) Autoscaler policy: target CPU/GPU utilization 55-70%; allow burst to shared spare capacity for 2m windows.
3) Model plan: evaluate these variants in the POC:
   - rwd-open-1.3B-quant (low cost) for baseline throughput
   - rwd-open-7B-q4 (balanced latency/cost) — primary candidate for short completions
   - rwd-open-13B-q8 (fallback for quality-critical flows; expect higher latency/cost)
4) Observability: Datadog integration with per-route latency breakdown, token-level cost, and 95/99 percentiles; add SLO alerts at 95th >= 120ms and error-rate >0.5%.

POC deliverables (week 1-3):
- Week 1: infra build + model onboarding + perf harness (simulate peak/spike patterns).
- Week 2: run synthetic and replay tests; tuning of batch window / KV cache.
- Week 3: present results, cost projections, and production topology recommendation.

Questions / action items for Karthik: 
- Confirm which routes are latency-critical vs best-effort (Daniel hinted search + autocomplete are critical).
- Ask Daniel for expected percent of unique prompts vs repeated (affects cache effectiveness).
- Can we get the read-only Datadog token and a sample trace ID for one peak window?

I’ll draft the POC infra spec once Karthik confirms routes and we get the CSV.

-Mina

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@lumenlogic.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inference SLOs & deployment plan — LumenLogic discovery follow-up

Daniel — thanks for the quick reply and the CSV. That distribution is exactly what we need. Short replies to your question and next steps: 

Models we plan to test in POC (high level cost bands):
- rwd-open-1.3B-quant: very low cost (baseline), good for high-throughput but lower quality for longer responses.
- rwd-open-7B-q4: sweet spot for short completions; expected 95th latency in POC to be within target with proper batching/cache.
- rwd-open-13B-q8: quality baseline for fallback flows; will be used for a small % of traffic in tests.

What we need from you this week:
- The 14-day RPS CSV (received) + token-length CSV if available (helps tune batch window).
- Read-only Datadog token and one sample trace id for a recent peak (so we can map latency sources).

Confirmed timeline: POC kickoff week of Jun 26. Mina will send the infra spec and a proposed test schedule by Thu Jun 21. Marissa will include a dashboard template for the SLOs.

If this looks good I’ll put a short SOW for the POC in HubSpot and we’ll lock in the kickoff slot.

Best — Karthik

--
